skill.name: tasknotes
skill.description: Manage Obsidian TaskNotes tasks through the local TaskNotes HTTP API, including listing, creating, updating, deleting, statistics, and filter options.
skill.summary: Manage Obsidian TaskNotes tasks from Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through a local API.
skill.author: ArtemXTech

security_audit.summary: The skill is a legitimate Obsidian TaskNotes CLI, but it has real security surface: it loads a vault-root .env, reads API credentials, and sends HTTP requests to a local API that can create, update, and delete tasks. Most markdown backtick detections are false positives, and no prompt injection text was found. The main unresolved risk is unvalidated TASKNOTES_API_PORT, which can affect the parsed request host when an Authorization header is present.

remediation.issue: Unvalidated TASKNOTES_API_PORT is interpolated into the request URL.
remediation.suggestion: Parse TASKNOTES_API_PORT as an integer from 1 to 65535 before constructing BASE_URL, and reject nonnumeric values.

remediation.issue: The script loads a vault-root .env file before making API requests.
remediation.suggestion: Load only TaskNotes-specific settings from a dedicated config file, or document that the vault .env must not contain unrelated secrets.

remediation.issue: The CLI can update and delete local TaskNotes records.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before destructive actions, and show the task path before delete operations.

remediation.issue: Documentation instructs agents to run uv commands from the skill directory.
remediation.suggestion: Keep command arguments constrained by argparse, avoid shell interpolation, and document the local network and credential behavior clearly.

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated Local API Port Can Change Request Host
semantic_findings.description: TASKNOTES_API_PORT is inserted into the URL without numeric validation. A crafted port value can change the parsed host and send the Authorization header away from localhost.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code builds BASE_URL with an unvalidated environment value and passes headers containing the API key to requests.request. URL userinfo parsing makes host confusion possible if the port value is crafted.

content.value_statement: Task tracking in Obsidian can be slow when you switch between notes and planning tools. This skill lets Claude, Codex, and Claude Code manage TaskNotes tasks through the local API.
actual_capabilities: List TaskNotes tasks with status, project, priority, limit, and overdue filters.
Create tasks with title, project, priority, status, due date, scheduled date, contexts, estimate, and details.
Update existing tasks by path, including status, priority, title, dates, and details.
Delete TaskNotes tasks by task file path.
Show task statistics and available TaskNotes filter options.
Return agent-friendly structured output or human-readable tables.
limitations: Requires Obsidian running with the TaskNotes HTTP API enabled.
Designed for the local TaskNotes API on the configured localhost port.
Status, priority, and project values depend on the user TaskNotes settings.
Authentication depends on local environment configuration and is not managed by the skill.

use_cases.title: Review Daily Work
use_cases.description: List active or overdue TaskNotes tasks before choosing the next work item.

use_cases.title: Capture Project Tasks
use_cases.description: Create linked project tasks with priority, due dates, and supporting details from a chat session.

use_cases.title: Keep Coding Work Visible
use_cases.description: Let an AI coding assistant update task status as implementation work moves forward.
use_cases.target_user: Developer using Claude Code or Codex

prompt_templates.title: Show Current Tasks
prompt_templates.prompt: List my open TaskNotes tasks. Use table output and include status, priority, title, project, and due date when available.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Project Task
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a TaskNotes task titled "Prepare release notes" for project "Website Redesign" with high priority and a due date tomorrow.

prompt_templates.title: Update Work Status
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the task path for "Prepare release notes", mark it done, and show a short confirmation with the updated status.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Focus Session
prompt_templates.prompt: List overdue and high-priority tasks, check available statuses if needed, then recommend the next five tasks to work on.

output_examples.output: A readable table of matching tasks with status, priority, title, project, and total count.

output_examples.input: Create a high-priority task for Website Redesign due tomorrow.
output_examples.output: A confirmation with the created task title, file path, status, and priority.

output_examples.input: What statuses, priorities, and projects can I use?
output_examples.output: A grouped list of available TaskNotes projects, statuses, and priorities from the local API.

best_practices: Run the options command before using custom status or priority values.
Use table output when a human needs to review tasks before action.
Keep the TaskNotes API token limited to this local workflow.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill when Obsidian or the TaskNotes API is not running.
Do not keep unrelated secrets in the same vault environment file.
Do not delete or overwrite tasks without confirming the task path first.

faq.question: Does this skill require Obsidian?
faq.answer: Yes. Obsidian must be running with the TaskNotes HTTP API enabled.

faq.question: Can it create and update tasks?
faq.answer: Yes. It can create, update, delete, list, and inspect TaskNotes tasks through the local API.

faq.question: Where does authentication come from?
faq.answer: It can read TASKNOTES_API_KEY from a local environment file when TaskNotes authentication is enabled.

faq.question: Can it connect to remote task services?
faq.answer: No. The documented design targets the local TaskNotes API on localhost.

faq.question: Does it know my custom TaskNotes values?
faq.answer: It can request available statuses, priorities, and projects from the TaskNotes API.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
